ttt_background_paragraph: I have been invited to participate to the 2025 edition of the Fête de la Science in the University of Strasbourg. I co-animated a computer science stand whose objective was to explain the concept of artificial intelligence (AI) using two workshops of unplugged computing (without computer of screen). Our stand was titled Come defy our cardboard AI !. We presented two workshops showcasing the concepts of artificial learning : the tic-tac-toe game and the game of Nim. This page is dedicated to the tic-tac-toe game; the game of Nim can be consulted on this page.
ttt_rules_paragraph: The tic-tac-toe game is played on a 3 by 3 board composed of empty tiles. Two players play each other and are represented by tokens, usually an X and an O. The game principle is quite simple : each player has to place one of its token in any free tile of the board. The final objective is to obtain a line composed of 3 identical tokens in any direction (vertical, horizontal or diagonal). The first player to achieve such line wins the game. In the event that all tiles are filled with a token and no 3 tokens alignement can be reached, the game ends in a tie. Using the following two animations, I propose a numerical version of the tic-tac-toe workshop divided in two variants (when the AI starts and when the human starts).
ttt_1_description: In this version, the AI is represented by the X tokens and the human player by the O tokens. The AI starts the game. The diagram on the right represents the bahaviour adopted by the AI when choosing where to place the next token. In a way, it shows a visualisation of how the AI 'thinks' in each situation/turn. Depending of the current configuration of the board, the AI adopts the behaviour described in the diagram. For instance, the AI starts by placing its X token on the first tile (topmost leftmost position) as indicated on the greatest scale of the diagram (topmost leftmost red X). If the human player plays its token right of the AI's, according to the diagram, the IA will play its next token on the center leftmost tile. This configuration corresponds to the situation illustrated at the second greatest scale in the diagram (topmost center tile).
ttt_2_description: In this version, the AI is represented by the O tokens and the human player by the X tokens. The human starts the game. The diagram on the right represents the bahaviour adopted by the AI when choosing where to place the next token. In a way, it shows a visualisation of how the AI 'thinks' in each situation/turn. Depending of the current configuration of the board, the AI adopts the behaviour described in the diagram. For instance, if the human player starts by placing its X token on the topmost leftmost tile, then the AI will place its O token at the center of the board as described in the diagram. This corresponds to the situation illustrated at the greatest scale (topmost leftmost tile) in the diagram.
